author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be filtered on one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory — the reader's page and the machine-readable document — accept a specialty filter and list only the veterinarians holding that specialty. Whole-name match, letter case ignored. A blank filter or none behaves as today.
acceptance_criteria: Filtered on a specialty some vets hold, the vet list page lists only those vets, still a page at a time.
Filtered on the same specialty, the machine-readable vet list carries only those vets.
A specialty differing from the stored name only by letter case filters the same vets.
A fragment of a specialty name filters no vets: matching is on the whole name.
On a filtered page with more vets than fit, moving to the next page keeps the filter applied.
A specialty no vet holds yields the normal page or document with an empty vet list and a success response, not an error.
An empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as if no filter were given, as an empty owner search does.
With no specialty given, both forms list every vet exactly as before.
Neither form gains a form, dropdown, or other on-page control for choosing the specialty.
non_goals: An on-page control for choosing the specialty — form, dropdown, or link (NG-10, deferred to a possible follow-up request).
Free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits (NG-9 holds outside this narrowing).
Filtering the directory on any attribute other than specialty.
Filtering more than one specialty at a time.
Paging the machine-readable directory: it carries the whole filtered list, as it carries the whole list today.
notes: PRD updated: NG-9 narrowed and NG-10 added; REQ-VET-003 mints the machine-readable directory as a supported surface (withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, its removal cancelled, ID not reused); new non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-vet-directory-specialty-filter.md; 'Specialty filter' added to docs/ubiquitous-language.md. Owner's stated surface contract, quoted from intake:1 so the design stage has it: '/vets.html?specialty=<name>' and '/vets?specialty=<name>', 'Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix', empty result is 'HTTP 200'. Two items outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new ADR, and system-design.md#contracts needs REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VETSSPECIALTYFILTER-001 mapped onto the vet contracts (Vets currently maps to no requirement). Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than consulted, per the intake: whether an unknown specialty name deserves an answer distinct from an empty result, and whether the machine-readable directory should page.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter stays inside the vet feature package and adds no type: two declared read methods on VetRepository, an optional request parameter on both VetController routes, and the parameter carried through the vetList pagination links. Two decisions were new ground and are now recorded. Case folding happens in the repository query, not in any vendor schema, because collation-based matching is what makes owner search vendor-divergent (system-design.md#persistence, ADR 2026-08-15-query-level-case-folding-for-specialty-match). The filtered reads carry no cache annotation, because the vets cache has no size bound and the specialty value is unauthenticated caller text (ADR 2026-08-15-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache). Contracts now map REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VETSSPECIALTYFILTER-001 onto Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, and VetController; the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less was removed, since REQ-VET-003 mints it. Claims resolved by reading the five vet sources, the three schema.sql files, CacheConfiguration, and build.gradle; no IDE oracle was connected, so this is the weaker grep-and-read basis.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two declared methods: a paged specialty-filtered read for the HTML route and an unpaged one for the machine-readable route. The interface extends the bare Repository marker, so an undeclared method does not exist.

Both VetController routes take an optional specialty request parameter. A null, empty, or whitespace-only value routes to the existing unfiltered method, so the no-filter path is byte-identical to today.
vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty through. Five links hard-code /vets.html?page=N today.
The machine-readable route keeps returning the whole filtered list in one Vets document; it does not page (prd-entry non-goal).

patterns.description: blank query parameter stripped and treated as the broadest result — the precedent for a blank specialty. Copy the normalization only: the owner path rejects an empty result with a binding error, which this slice must not do.
existing showVetList and its findPaginated helper — the filtered path branches inside the helper, keeping the page-size and model-attribute shape unchanged
declared-method repository over the Repository marker; the two cached methods are the ones the filtered additions must not imitate

risks.risk: A paged derived query joining the EAGER many-to-many can make Hibernate apply the limit in memory (HHH90003004) instead of in SQL, silently defeating paging.
risks.mitigation: Assert page size and total pages in the pagination test rather than only the filtered contents; if the warning appears, declare an explicit query with a matching countQuery.

risks.risk: The join emits a vet once per matching specialty row, so two specialty rows whose names differ only by case would duplicate a vet and skew the page count.
risks.mitigation: Seeded specialty names are distinct; if that stops holding, select distinct roots.

risks.risk: The specialty value is caller-supplied text reflected into the pagination hrefs. Concatenating it into the URL string, as the template's current __${i}__ preprocessing does for the page number, skips URL encoding.
risks.mitigation: Build the links with Thymeleaf's link-parameter syntax so the engine encodes the value and omits the parameter when it is absent.

risks.risk: Annotating the filtered reads @Cacheable('vets') would look consistent with their siblings and would let any caller insert unbounded entries into a cache with no size limit.
risks.mitigation: The two filtered methods carry no cache annotation; the ADR and the threat-model row record why.

risks.risk: Deciding the match in the controller or the template would put a business rule in a web controller, which architecture-principles.md § pattern catalog admits no new instance of.
risks.mitigation: Selection lives in the repository query. Stripping a blank parameter is request binding, not a rule, and stays in the controller as it does for owner search.

notes: Both items the product expert flagged as outside its write scope are done: docs/adr/README.md now indexes the non-goal ADR (plus the two ADRs this triage wrote), and system-design.md#contracts maps REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VETSSPECIALTYFILTER-001 onto the five vet contracts — Vets no longer maps to a dash. Removing the stale Known Defects row made the top provenance note's 'four behaviors' count wrong; it now reads three, and gained a clause covering post-survey statements. Overview now names the machine-readable directory as the one supported non-HTML surface. Open questions recorded rather than consulted, per the owner's standing instruction: (1) whether the vets cache should carry a size bound, which is the only thing keeping the filtered reads uncached — added to system-design.md § Open Questions from the Survey item 5; (2) the two product questions the PRD already carries (a distinct answer for an unknown specialty, and paging the machine-readable directory) are taken at their narrowest here — empty list with a success response, and no paging. No design-doc-autofix records exist, so the autofix audit found nothing. scripts/doctor.py check reports one pre-existing failure, 'project-data: spec_version 0.1.0 does not match manifest 0.2.0', unrelated to this slice and outside my write scope.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: No NVD match was run in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access. Resolved versions read from ./gradlew --offline dependencies for the record — Spring Boot 4.1.0, spring-web 7.0.8, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.4. Treat the framework-CVE check as not verified; a human or CI closes it. Since this change set alters no dependency, nothing here is a regression introduced by the slice.

The encoding regression test uses "surgery & pain". Adding one payload containing a double quote and angle brackets (for example 'a"><script>') would pin the property that actually matters — the value cannot terminate the href attribute — rather than only ampersand-and-space encoding. Offered to the test-reviewer as coverage depth, not a defect: the current implementation encodes such a payload correctly.

The specialty parameter has no maximum length. The servlet container's request-line limit bounds it in practice, so no unbounded allocation is reachable, but if a future change moves the filter to a POST body that bound disappears.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the filter reaches the database only through the two Spring Data derived methods VetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and (String). No query text is concatenated; IgnoreCase folds case inside the generated, parameterized query. Matches the SQL-injection mitigation in system-design.md#threat-model and the injection row of security-principles.md.

Reflected XSS through the pagination links: all five vetList.html anchors moved from the __${...}__ preprocessing form to the engine link form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}. The engine URL-encodes the parameter value and Thymeleaf's default attribute escaping stays on, so caller text cannot break out of the href. VetControllerTests pins both the unfiltered shape (no specialty= emitted) and the encoded shape ("surgery & pain" renders as specialty=surgery%20%26%20pain). Verified against the resolved Thymeleaf version on the runtime classpath, org.thymeleaf:thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, which is the version the ADR's empty-collection behaviour is claimed for.

Preprocessing sweep: grep over src/main/resources/templates finds no __${...}__ occurrence carrying a request-derived value. The remaining occurrences in owners/ownersList.html are outside this change set and interpolate integers (currentPage, totalPages) and a persisted owner id, not caller text. This change strictly reduces the preprocessing surface.

Cache safety: the two filtered reads carry no @Cacheable, so no cache key derives from caller-supplied text. The vets cache has no size bound, so this is the correct choice and it closes the unbounded-cache-growth row of the threat model rather than widening it (ADR 2026-08-15-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-bypass-the-cache). The bypass costs an uncached database read per filtered request on an already-open route; that is ordinary read load on a route that was already reachable, not a new amplification primitive, since one request still yields one bounded page query.

Boundary normalization: VetController.specialtyFilter treats null, empty, and whitespace-only alike and returns null, so the unfiltered path is byte-identical to the previous behaviour on both routes. No null dereference is reachable (List.of(filter) is guarded by the null check).

Exposed surface: no new route and no new dependency. Both routes are pre-existing and already unauthenticated per system-design.md#security-context; the change adds an optional read-only query parameter to each, exposing no data a caller could not already retrieve unfiltered. No mass-assignment surface (no request-bound type added), no file or resource path composed from input, no deserialization entry point, no logging, no shell or process execution, no secret-shaped literal anywhere in the diff.
Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged, so no dependency is added, removed, or version-shifted by this change set.

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet feature package and its template: three production files in one module, two derived repository reads, an optional query parameter on two pre-existing routes, no sensitive paths, and no dependency or schema change; the remaining ten files are docs and ADRs.

semantic_surprise.note: A specialty no vet holds makes the page render an empty Page whose getTotalPages() is 0 (size 5, total 0), and vetList.html iterates #numbers.sequence(1, totalPages); Thymeleaf 3.1.5 NumberUtils.sequence steps -1 when from is greater than to, so sequence(1, 0) yields [1, 0] and the page emits a link to /vets.html?page=0&specialty=..., which reaches PageRequest.of(-1, 5) and throws, so the empty-result path the PRD requires to be presented normally hands the reader a one-click failure.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are otherwise real: the repository tests run against a live schema and pin case folding, whole-name matching, and true paging, and the controller tests assert rendered link text rather than restating the code. But the empty-result controller test stubs new PageImpl of an empty list, which is unpaged, so getSize() is 0 and getTotalPages() returns 1 instead of the production 0, and the mock shape hides exactly the pagination render that breaks.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round two is unanimous with empty findings, but the security approval, its only verdict, parks three caveats and one is explicitly unclosed: no NVD match was run, so the framework-CVE check is recorded as not verified and left to a human or CI, alongside an unbounded parameter length and a request for a quote-and-angle-bracket XSS payload; code quality's first-round approval also parked two style recommendations.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the intake exactly: an optional URL parameter on both surfaces, pagination links carrying it, and no form or dropdown on either page, with NG-9 narrowed, NG-10 recorded, and REQ-VET-003 minted rather than the withdrawn id reused; the one design revision and the single build retry were ADR-coverage bookkeeping in the autofix audit, not scope drift.

rationale: Read the empty-result path before merging. A specialty nobody holds yields totalPages 0, and Thymeleaf's sequence(1, 0) counts down, so the page renders a link to page=0 that throws inside PageRequest. The controller test's unpaged PageImpl reports one page and hides it.
